# Database Connection Configuration

This module (`src/config/database.js`) is responsible for establishing and managing the connection to your MongoDB database using the Mongoose ODM. It provides a robust and centralized way for your application to interact with the backend data store.

## Overview

The `database.js` file exports a single asynchronous function, `connectDB`, which initializes the connection to MongoDB. This function is typically called once at application startup (e.g., in `src/app.js`) to ensure that all subsequent database operations performed by models (like `src/models/user.js` or `src/models/chat.js`) have a live connection available.

## Setup

Before connecting to the database, you must configure your MongoDB connection string as an environment variable.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create or locate your .env file">
    Ensure you have a `.env` file in the root of your project. This file is used to store environment-specific variables, including sensitive credentials.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add DB_CONNECTION_SECRET to .env">
    Open your `.env` file and add the `DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` variable, setting its value to your MongoDB connection string.
    <Warning>
      Never hardcode your `DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` directly in your source code. Always use environment variables for sensitive information like database credentials and API keys.
    </Warning>
    ```dotenv
    DB_CONNECTION_SECRET="mongodb+srv://<username>:<password>@<cluster-name>.mongodb.net/<database-name>?retryWrites=true&w=majority"
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Obtain your MongoDB connection string">
    If you are using MongoDB Atlas, log in to your Atlas dashboard, navigate to your cluster, and click "Connect". Choose "Connect your application" to get your connection string. Remember to replace `<username>`, `<password>`, and `<database-name>` with your actual credentials and desired database name.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Install Mongoose">
    Ensure Mongoose is installed as a dependency in your project.
    ```bash
    npm install mongoose
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## connectDB Function

The `connectDB` function is an asynchronous operation that attempts to establish a connection to the MongoDB database using the provided `DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` environment variable.

<Note>
  Upon successful connection, Mongoose will handle keeping the connection alive for your application. If the connection fails, it will log the error to the console.
</Note>

<ParamField name="DB_CONNECTION_SECRET" type="string" required>
  This is the environment variable that holds your full MongoDB connection URI. It's automatically accessed by the function.
  <Warning>
    Exposing `DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` in client-side code or public repositories poses a severe security risk. Ensure it is only accessible server-side.
  </Warning>
</ParamField>

<ResponseField name="void" type="Promise<void>">
  This function does not return any explicit value on success. It establishes a side-effect of connecting to the database. It throws an error if the connection fails.
</ResponseField>

### Usage Example

The `connectDB` function is typically imported and called once at the start of your application, for instance, in `src/app.js`, to ensure the database is ready before handling any requests.

```javascript filename="src/app.js"
const express = require('express');
const connectDB = require('./config/database'); // Import the connectDB function
require('dotenv').config(); // Load environment variables from .env file

const app = express();

// Connect to the database
connectDB()
  .then(() => {
    console.log('MongoDB Connected...');
    const PORT = process.env.PORT || 5000;
    app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`Server running on port ${PORT}`));
  })
  .catch(err => {
    console.error('Database connection failed:', err);
    process.exit(1); // Exit process with failure
  });

// Other middleware and route definitions for app...
// app.use('/api/users', require('./routes/user'));
```

## Common Errors / Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="DB_CONNECTION_SECRET is undefined or missing">
    <Danger>
      If `process.env.DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` is not set, the `mongoose.connect` call will fail, leading to an application crash or an unhandled promise rejection.
    </Danger>
    **Solution:**
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Verify .env file">
        Ensure you have a `.env` file in your project root.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Check variable name">
        Double-check that the variable in your `.env` file is exactly `DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` and not misspelled.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Load .env variables">
        Make sure you are loading environment variables at the start of your application (e.g., `require('dotenv').config();`).
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Invalid MongoDB connection string">
    If the connection string provided in `DB_CONNECTION_SECRET` is malformed, uses incorrect credentials, or points to an unreachable server, Mongoose will fail to connect.
    **Solution:**
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Check credentials">
        Verify that the username and password in your connection string are correct and have the necessary database access privileges.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Verify cluster address">
        Ensure the cluster address (`<cluster-name>.mongodb.net`) is accurate.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Network access">
        If connecting from a restricted environment, ensure your IP address is whitelisted in your MongoDB Atlas (or self-hosted) network access settings.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Database availability">
        Confirm that your MongoDB instance or cluster is running and accessible.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Mongoose connection error messages">
    Mongoose often provides descriptive error messages. Pay close attention to the `err` object logged by the `.catch` block in your application startup.
    <Tip>
      Common errors include `MongooseServerSelectionError` (network or server availability issues) or `MongoNetworkError` (firewall or incorrect host).
    </Tip>
    **Solution:**
    Consult the official Mongoose documentation or MongoDB error code references for specific error messages to diagnose further.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
